answer: A spiral of escalating verification stops cheap identity farming: new agents start with a tiny transaction limit and earn larger caps only through months of attested, useful work. A vault holds a refundable bond behind each identity, forfeited if the agent is caught running duplicates. Like saffron, genuine reputation is costly to grow and easy to spot when faked, so an attacker must pay real money and time per fake identity instead of spawning them for free.
